source_span: We sized the US data center power shortfall at 57 GW from 2026-28. We forecast this is 32 GW net of time to power solutions, which translates to a 34% net US power shortfall through 2028.
source_chain: A: US data centers face a 57GW gross / 32GW net power shortfall through 2028, so only large credit-worthy hyperscalers/neoclouds can secure energization (60-95% of global DC capacity adds) THEREFORE B: power scarcity, not chip supply, becomes the binding constraint, putting memory/optical/analog components and ASICs (lower tokens/GW than GPUs) at risk while NVDA/AVGO stay protected through 2027 THEREFORE C: MS cuts its US share of global compute forecast to 55% from 60% since overseas capacity can only partly offset the gap. Invalidation (stated in the note): the shortfall narrows only if behind-the-meter power (turbines, fuel cells, nuclear) or international expansion materialize faster than modeled — and the note explicitly argues international capacity is not enough to absorb the US shortfall.
pulse_chain: A: MS sizes the power gap (57GW gross/32GW net, developers short 32-42GW = 34-43% of demand) as the binding constraint on the AI buildout through 2028 THEREFORE B: utilities will energize only credit-worthy buyers, so the largest clouds and AI-only clouds take 60-95% of global DC capacity THEREFORE C: disruption lands on memory/optics/small-dollar components and ASICs risk losing share to GPUs; MS cuts US compute share to 55% from 60%. The pulse then sets Goldman's Dell/memory read as the counter-argument and makes TSM's Oct 15 capex guidance ($85B 2027/$98B 2028) the condition that decides between a power-constrained read and an equipment-constrained read.
why: The pulse reproduces MS's A-through-C chain faithfully but swaps the note's own stated invalidation (the shortfall narrows only if behind-the-meter power or international expansion outpaces the modeled gap, which MS says won't happen) for an unrelated condition it invents — TSM's capex guidance deciding between a 'power-constrained' and 'equipment-constrained' read.
